### Phasor Representation of Alternating Quantities
An alternating quantity (sinusoidal voltage or current) is given by:
$$v(t) = V_m \sin(\omega t + \theta)$|

Using Euler's identity, this can be projected as the imaginary part of a rotating complex vector (phasor):
$$\vec{V} = V_{rms} \angle \theta = V_{rms}(\cos\theta + j\sin\theta)$$

Thus, a sinusoidal time-varying wave is compactly represented by a stationary vector (phasor) having magnitude equal to RMS value and phase angle relative to the reference axis.
proTip: Phasors simplify AC calculations by converting differential equations into simple algebraic complex number operations.
